subject: Capacity rebaseline: Halcyon renewal — conversion-factor modeling & GPU fingerprinting
messages:
From: Sera Patel <sera@halcyonai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@halcyonai.com, anand.reddy@halcyonai.com
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — usage spike and ask for sizing guidance

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Hope you both had a good week. Our renewal for the Dedicated GPU contract is coming up (end of May) and we've observed a steady 38% increase in peak token throughput over the last quarter (attached CSV). Given that growth profile, procurement is asking for a concrete plan that maps our usage to committed capacity and a ramp schedule that avoids service interruptions.

As background: our prod traffic is spiky — long-tail LLM chat workloads during North American business hours — and we've started a small A/B test of a 13B parameter model that is 1.8x more GPU-intensive than our previous baseline. We need recommendations on:

- How many additional GPUs to commit for the 12‑month renewal term (and staging windows),
- Whether to do a multi-tranche onboarding (staggered vs. all-at-once),
- Short-term burst/auto-burst options while we finalize commit,
- Any data or profiling you need from our side to make a deterministic sizing recommendation.

We want to balance cost predictability with the flexibility to scale during the launch of the new model. Can we get your proposed approach and a 1-page runbook that procurement can attach to the renewal?

Thanks,
Sera
Product Ops — Halcyon AI

Attachments: Halcyon_usage_May2026.csv (sampled token/tps by hour)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sera Patel <sera@halcyonai.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — usage spike and ask for sizing guidance

Sera — thanks for the data, this is exactly what we need. High level recommendation approach below; I'll follow up with a short attached workbook that captures the conversion-factor model we use to translate token/sec into equivalent GPU-days.

1) Conversion-factor modeling: we’ll run a model fingerprinting pass against a representative sample of your traces to compute a per-model conversion factor (relative GPU cost vs. your baseline). That gives deterministic sizing rather than a blunt tokens->GPUs estimate. I attached the initial workbook (conversion_model_v1.xlsx) — we can populate it together.

2) Multi-tranche onboarding: strong preference for a staggered tranche (30/50/20) over three weeks. This lets us validate KV cache behavior and tail latency while keeping commit exposure limited.

3) Canary & autoscale buffer: recommend reserving a 15% autoscale buffer on top of the tranche to cover daily peaks. For the initial term we can include burst credits (transient GPU usage) for the first 60 days while you complete model optimization.

4) Observability & regressions: we’ll add a prompt set and latency budget checks into the renewal runbook; if model-level latency regresses we’ll automatically trigger a rollback to a cheaper variant.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben, can you run a quick fingerprint job on the attached sample traces and share the per-model factors?
- Karthik, ops input on tranche scheduling and pre-warm steps (network warmup / image prefetch).
- Sera, procurement wants a 1-page runbook + a proposed ramp schedule by next Friday (26th).

I’ll assemble the runbook draft and send to procurement once we have the conversion numbers.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Sera Patel <sera@halcyonai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — usage spike and ask for sizing guidance

Adding technical detail from infra / fleet perspective. I've started the fingerprinting run (small sample first) — initial numbers indicate the new 13B model maps to ~1.75 conversion factor relative to Halcyon's baseline model. From that:

- Immediate recommendation: add 18 GPUs to committed capacity and stage as tranches: 6 -> 9 -> 3 across three weeks. That gives ~40% headroom for the first 90 days including a 15% buffer.
- Alternative (lower commitment): commit 12 GPUs + a 20% monthly burst pool for the first quarter while optimization continues. This is a cheaper commit but carries more burst management overhead.
- Ops notes: pre-warm image layers and prime KV caches 48 hours before each tranche; expect elevated token costs during the warm windows. Laura, can you draft the operational checklist for pre-warm and rollback?

Attachments referenced: tranche_addendum.pdf (staging checklist & rollback timings).

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
From: Sera Patel <sera@halcyonai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@halcyonai.com, anand.reddy@halcyonai.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 06:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — usage spike and ask for sizing guidance

Team — this is really helpful, thanks. Procurement prefers the 18 GPU committed path with the 6/9/3 tranche schedule; that fits our forecast and gives us predictable unit economics. Two quick asks before we finalize:

1) Can you turn the conversion_model_v1.xlsx into a single-sheet summary (one page) that procurement can include in the contract? We need the mapping and an example calculation (current avg tps -> GPUs committed).
2) Please include the DocuSign-ready clause language for the 15% autoscale buffer and the 60-day burst credits so our legal team can review.

If you send the runbook + one-pager and the contract clause, procurement will start the internal approvals and I’ll route the DocuSign. We can target signing the amendment by 1 April to allow provisioning time.

Thanks again — Sera

Procurement note: procurement@halcyonai.com will handle routing once you send the summary and clause.

--
Sera Patel
Product Ops — Halcyon AI
